items.question: Which of these is a metal?
items.explanation: Iron is a metal: it is hard, shiny when polished and conducts heat and electricity. Sulphur, carbon and oxygen are non-metals. Iron is used to make bridges, tools and cooking pans.

items.question: Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.
items.explanation: Almost all metals are solid at room temperature, but mercury is a liquid. It was used in old thermometers. Mercury is poisonous, so it should never be touched.

items.question: Iron rusts when it comes in contact with:
items.explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen and water (or moisture). Rust is a reddish-brown layer called iron oxide. Painting or oiling iron keeps air and water away, so it does not rust.

items.question: Metals that can be beaten into thin sheets are called ___.
items.explanation: Malleable means it can be hammered into thin sheets without breaking. Aluminium foil used to wrap food is a good example. Most non-metals, like sulphur, break instead.

items.question: Which non-metal is a good conductor of electricity?
items.explanation: Most non-metals do not conduct electricity, but graphite (a form of carbon) does. That is why it is used in some batteries. The "lead" in your pencil is actually graphite.
